data.gender_notes: Shalin is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Shalin is of Sanskrit origin, meaning 'Mountain of Shining Pearls'. It is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Shaila' meaning mountain and 'Ankusha' meaning pearl. This name is often given to a child born during the night of the new moon and is believed to bring peace and calmness to the family. The name Shalin carries the meaning “Mountain of Shining Pearls” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shalin usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain of shining pearls and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shalin is a divine name that represents the strength and resilience of a mountain, as well as the purity and brilliance of a pearl. It is a name that is deeply rooted in Hindu spirituality and is often associated with peace, calmness, and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Shalin belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mountain of Shining Pearls.”

The addition of the word 'pearl' further enhances the name's significance, representing the individual's inner beauty, value, and worth.
